clause.api-endpoint.client-changes.state: Changes to calling clients are not included.
clause.api-endpoint.contract-honoured.st: When a valid call is made according to the agreed contract, then the response shall contain the specified fields with the correct types and status code.
clause.api-endpoint.contract-honoured.ve: Calls are run against the verification environment by the verifier.
clause.api-endpoint.error-codes.statemen: When an invalid call is made, then the response shall carry the defined error code and a readable explanation — never an unformatted server error.
clause.api-endpoint.error-codes.verifica: One call per defined error case.
When the caller lacks authorisation, then the call shall be refused and no data disclosed.
Calls without authorisation and with the wrong authorisation.
clause.automation.alerts-on-failure.stat: When a run fails, then an alert shall go to the agreed recipient.
clause.automation.alerts-on-failure.veri: A run is made to fail deliberately during verification.
clause.automation.manual-rerun.statement: The customer can rerun the job manually according to the accompanying instructions.
clause.automation.manual-rerun.verificat: The customer reruns a run during verification.
clause.automation.monitoring-setup.state: Monitoring tools and on-call routines are not included.
clause.automation.runs-on-schedule.state: The job runs according to the specified schedule in the specified environment, evidenced by at least two runs.
clause.automation.runs-on-schedule.verif: The runs are visible in the log with time and outcome.
clause.base.clean-start.statement: The code can be started from a clean state according to the accompanying instructions.
clause.base.clean-start.verification: The supplier demonstrates a start in a freshly set-up environment.
clause.base.clock-stop.statement: If the customer does not deliver on their commitments, the delivery time is paused day by day until the commitment is met.
clause.base.data-cleanup.statement: Correction of the customer's existing data is not included.
clause.base.dependency-licenses.statemen: Added third-party dependencies are listed with their licence.
clause.base.error-handling.statement: The application does not crash on foreseeable error cases — the errors are handled and reported.
clause.base.error-handling.verification: The error cases listed among the criteria are run.
clause.base.new-wishes.statement: Wishes that arise during the delivery are not included — they become a new gig.
clause.base.no-regressions.statement: No functionality that existed before the delivery stops working.
clause.base.no-regressions.verification: The customer's existing smoke-test list is run after the delivery.
clause.base.no-secrets.statement: No secrets, keys or passwords are present in the source code or the repository.
clause.base.no-secrets.verification: A scan of the repository and its history.
clause.base.ongoing-support.statement: Ongoing maintenance, support and on-call duty after the warranty period are not included.
clause.base.rejection-cites-rows.stateme: A rejection shall state which criteria lines are not met, not a general expression of dissatisfaction.
clause.base.silent-acceptance.statement: No response within the acceptance window counts as approval.
clause.base.third-party-changes.statemen: Changes to systems the customer does not control are not included.
clause.base.training.statement: Training of the customer's staff is not included.
clause.base.warranty.statement: Deviations from approved acceptance criteria are corrected free of charge within 30 days of acceptance. New wishes are not warranty matters — they are new gigs.
clause.bugfix.investigation-cap.statemen: If the fault has not been located within the specified cap on hours, the assignment stops, and the parties agree on a paid troubleshooting gig before work continues.
clause.bugfix.neighbours-intact.statemen: The specified adjacent functions work unchanged.
clause.bugfix.neighbours-intact.verifica: A walk-through of the list in the verification environment.
clause.bugfix.other-bugs.statement: Other faults discovered during the work are not included.
clause.bugfix.refactoring.statement: Rebuilding the surrounding code is not included.
clause.bugfix.regression-test.statement: A test that catches the fault exists, and it passes after the fix.
clause.bugfix.regression-test.verificati: The test is run against the code before and after the fix.
clause.bugfix.reproduction-gone.statemen: When the described reproduction case is run, then the fault shall no longer occur.
clause.bugfix.reproduction-gone.verifica: The verifier runs the steps in the specified environment.
clause.data-migration.bad-row-report.sta: Rows that could not be interpreted are listed in a report with the reason given per row.
clause.data-migration.bad-row-report.ver: The report is delivered together with the run.
clause.data-migration.count-reconciliati: When the migration has been run, then the number of records in the target shall match the source according to the agreed reconciliation, with every discrepancy explained.
Reconciliation report run in the verification environment.
clause.data-migration.ongoing-sync.state: Ongoing synchronisation after the migration is not included.
clause.data-migration.rerun-idempotent.s: When the migration is rerun against the same source, then the result shall be the same without duplicates.
clause.data-migration.rerun-idempotent.v: Two consecutive runs in the verification environment, with reconciliation after each.
clause.data-migration.source-cleanup.sta: Correction of faulty data in the source is not included.
clause.environment.application-adaptatio: Adaptations to the application resulting from the upgrade are not included, beyond those listed in the criteria.
clause.environment.rollback-documented.s: A documented way back exists, and it has been tested.
clause.environment.rollback-documented.v: The rollback is tested in the test environment before the production upgrade.
clause.environment.smoke-passes.statemen: Every item on the specified smoke-test list passes after the upgrade.
clause.environment.smoke-passes.verifica: The list is ticked off line by line.
clause.environment.version-live.statemen: The target environment runs the specified version, readable in the environment itself.
clause.environment.version-live.verifica: The version is read off in the target environment by the verifier.
clause.integration.historical-backfill.s: Transfer of historical data is not included — the integration applies from deployment onwards.
clause.integration.roundtrip.statement: When a real test case is sent in each agreed direction, then the receiving system shall contain the record with all agreed fields.
clause.integration.roundtrip.verificatio: Run in the verification environment by the designated verifier, with the customer's test data.
clause.integration.target-system-changes: Changes to the receiving system are not included, beyond configuration the customer controls themselves.
clause.integration.target-unavailable.st: When the target system does not respond, then the integration shall behave according to the agreed error handling without losing records.
clause.integration.target-unavailable.ve: Tested by switching off or redirecting the recipient during verification.
clause.integration.transfer-log.statemen: Every transfer is logged with time, number of records and outcome, and the customer can read the log.
clause.integration.transfer-log.verifica: The log lines are shown to the verifier after the test run.
clause.other.minimum-works.statement: What was specified as the minimum working scope works in the verification environment.
clause.other.minimum-works.verification: A walk-through against the answer to the question about minimum scope.
clause.performance.behaviour-unchanged.s: The functional outcome is unchanged before and after, for the specified cases.
clause.performance.behaviour-unchanged.v: Comparison of output before and after the optimisation.
clause.performance.infrastructure-cost.s: Expanded infrastructure and additional licence costs are not included.
clause.performance.target-reached.statem: When the measurement is run under the specified conditions, then the target value shall be reached.
clause.performance.target-reached.verifi: The same measurement method as the baseline, run by the verifier.
clause.report.filters-work.statement: Every filter gives the expected outcome for at least one test case specified in advance.
clause.report.filters-work.verification: One test case per filter, with the expected number of records stated before the run.
clause.report.matches-reference.statemen: When the report is run for the specified period, then every total shall match the reference calculation.
clause.report.matches-reference.verifica: Side by side against the reference, by the verifier.
clause.report.source-data-quality.statem: Correction of errors in the underlying data is not included — the report shows what the source contains.
clause.screen.appearance-basis.statement: The design is judged against the specified design basis. If no basis exists, the design is the supplier's choice and cannot on its own be grounds for rejection.
clause.screen.browsers-covered.statement: The view works in the specified browsers and screen sizes.
clause.screen.browsers-covered.verificat: The verifier opens the view in each of them.
clause.screen.content-production.stateme: Production of copy and images is not included.
clause.screen.design-work.statement: Production of graphic design or a design system is not included.
clause.screen.fields-present.statement: All the specified fields are present in the view, with the validation specified for each of them.
clause.screen.fields-present.verificatio: A field-by-field walk-through against the list in the specification.
clause.screen.validation-messages.statem: When invalid input is submitted, then a readable error message shall be shown at the field that is wrong.
clause.screen.validation-messages.verifi: One test case per validation rule.
clause.study.implementation.statement: Implementation of what the investigation proposes is not included.
clause.study.no-preference.statement: Whoever does the feasibility study has no priority on the build it leads to.
clause.study.questions-answered.statemen: Every question listed in advance is answered in the document, with a source or reasoning.
clause.study.questions-answered.verifica: A question-by-question walk-through against the list.
clause.study.recommendation-motivated.st: The recommendation is justified, and the alternatives that were rejected are presented with reasons.
clause.study.recommendation-motivated.ve: The section is read by the person who is to make the decision.
clause.study.spec-publishable.statement: If a specification is included, it meets gigga's formal requirements for publication.
clause.study.spec-publishable.verificati: The specification is trial-published in gigga.

question.automation.work.prompt: What is to be run, and what counts as a successful run?
question.base.acceptance-window-days.pro: How many working days do you have to approve or reject the delivery?
question.base.access-deadline.help: If they are late, the delivery time is paused day by day according to the clock-stop term.

question.base.deliverables.prompt: What is handed over, concretely? State the repository, the branch and how the delivery is made — pull request, tag or otherwise.

question.base.ip-owner.option.supplier-l: The supplier owns it, the customer gets a right of use

Yes, with a perpetual right of use for the customer

question.base.test-data.prompt: What test data is used, and who provides it?
question.base.verification-environment.h: This is the field most fixed-price deals founder on. "It works on my machine" is not grounds for acceptance.
question.base.verification-owner.prompt: Who runs the verification? State name and role.
question.base.verification-record.prompt: How is the result of the verification documented?
question.bugfix.code-access.option.delay: Yes, but it takes a few days
question.bugfix.code-access.option.no: No, the code is held by someone else
question.bugfix.code-access.prompt: Do you have access to the code to give?
question.bugfix.environment.prompt: In which environment does the fault occur?
The investigation time is unknown before one has started. The cap is the protection for both sides.
After how many hours of troubleshooting is the assignment to stop and be re-estimated?
question.bugfix.neighbours.prompt: Which adjacent functions are to keep working unchanged?
question.bugfix.reproduction.help: Without a reproduction case the assignment cannot be delimited, and then a fixed price cannot be set.
question.bugfix.reproduction.prompt: How is the fault reproduced, step by step?
question.bugfix.root-or-symptom.option.r: The cause, even if it takes longer
question.bugfix.root-or-symptom.option.s: The symptom is enough for now
question.bugfix.root-or-symptom.prompt: Is it the fault that is to go, or the symptom?
question.context.access.prompt: Who has access to code and environments today, and who decides on new access?
question.context.stack.prompt: What technical stack? State language, framework and database.
question.context.urgency.help: The answer says more about how pressing the assignment is than a date does.
question.context.urgency.prompt: What happens if this does not get done?
question.environment.access.option.custo: Only the customer — the supplier instructs
question.environment.access.prompt: Who has access to the target environment?
question.environment.downtime-window.pro: Which window applies for the downtime?
question.environment.infrastructure.prom: What infrastructure does it run on?
question.environment.smoke-list.prompt: Which smoke-test list is to pass after the upgrade?
question.integration.direction.option.in: From the other system into yours
question.integration.direction.option.ou: From your system to the recipient
question.integration.direction.prompt: In which direction does the data flow?
question.integration.frequency.help: For example on every event, every five minutes, or once a night.
question.integration.frequency.prompt: How often is data to be transferred?
question.integration.on-failure.prompt: What is to happen when the recipient does not respond?
question.integration.protocol.help: For example REST over HTTPS with OAuth2, SFTP with a key, or a message queue.
question.integration.protocol.prompt: What protocol and what authentication are used?
question.integration.systems.prompt: Which two systems are to be connected?
No, but the system's vendor answers questions
question.integration.target-docs.prompt: Is there documentation for the receiving system?
question.integration.test-environments.p: Is there a test environment on both sides?
question.migration.bad-rows.option.best-: Loaded as far as possible and flagged
question.migration.bad-rows.option.rejec: Rejected and reported, the rest continue
question.migration.bad-rows.prompt: What is to happen with rows that cannot be interpreted?
The supplier, as part of the assignment
question.migration.source.prompt: From which source, and in what format?
question.migration.volume.prompt: Approximate data volume — number of records and size?
question.other.disappointment.help: The question captures the unspoken, and the unspoken is what sinks fixed-price deals.
question.other.disappointment.prompt: What would disappoint you even though everything you asked for has been delivered?
question.other.done-definition.prompt: Describe how you will decide whether this is done.
question.other.minimum-viable.prompt: What is the least that must work for you to pay?
question.performance.baseline.prompt: What is the baseline value, with unit?
question.performance.behaviour-change.op: Yes, if the change is approved in advance
No, the outcome must be identical
Yes, within the scope of the assignment
question.performance.behaviour-change.pr: May the behaviour change in order to reach the target?
question.performance.load.prompt: Under what load and with what data volume is it measured?
question.performance.slow-today.help: This type must never be left without a measured baseline. "Faster" cannot be verified.
question.performance.slow-today.prompt: What is slow today, and how has it been measured?
question.performance.target.prompt: What is the target value, with unit?
question.report.figures.prompt: Which figures are to be shown, from which sources, and with which filters?
question.report.format.prompt: In what format is the result to be delivered?
question.report.verification-period.prom: Which period and which data selection are used in the verification?
question.screen.browsers.prompt: Which browsers are to be supported?
question.screen.design-source.prompt: Where is the basis, and who decides on departures from it?
question.screen.design.help: Disputes about this type are almost always about appearance. Either there is a sketch, or the design is explicitly the supplier's choice.
question.screen.design.option.design-sys: An existing design system to follow
question.screen.design.option.free: None — the design is the supplier's choice
question.screen.fields.prompt: Which fields are to be present, and what validation applies to each of them?
question.screen.mobile.prompt: Is the view to work on mobile?
question.screen.roles.prompt: Which roles are to see the view?
question.shared.alert-target.help: Name or function plus channel — email, chat, telephone. "Someone in operations" cannot be verified.
question.shared.alert-target.prompt: Who is to be alerted when something goes wrong, and on which channel?
question.shared.reference-result.help: This question captures unspoken expectations, and the unspoken is what sinks fixed-price deals.
question.shared.reference-result.prompt: Is there something similar that already works, which the result can be compared with?
question.shared.rerun-allowed.prompt: May the delivery be rerun without creating duplicates or other side effects?
question.shared.rollback-plan.prompt: Is a documented way back needed if something goes wrong, and who carries it out?
question.study.audience.prompt: Who is to read the result?
question.study.format.prompt: In what form is the result delivered?
question.study.questions.help: The list is the delivery itself — acceptance becomes that each of the questions is answered.
question.study.questions.prompt: Which questions are to be answered? Number them.
question.study.recommendation.prompt: Is the result to contain a recommendation?
question.study.spec-output.prompt: Is the investigation to result in a specification that can be used for the next gig?
requestDetail.noBidsBuyer: No bids have been submitted yet.
requestDetail.noPermissions: No one else has read access.
requestDetail.permissionsLede: Whoever you invite can reach the request, the bids and their documents — but can neither submit a bid, sign, nor invite others.
requestDetail.specMissingDetail: No one can submit a bid until you have said what kind of assignment it is, answered the questions and approved the acceptance criteria.
requestDetail.specMissingTitle: The specification has not been finalised.
requestDetail.specReadBeforePricing: Read through the lines before you set a price.
requestDetail.specReadingLede: This is what the bid covers.
requestDetail.specUnpublishedDetail: The assignment is not open for bids until the scope and the acceptance criteria have been published.

requestSpec.addCriterionHeading: Add a line of your own
requestSpec.chooseTypesHeading: What kind of assignment is it?
requestSpec.chooseTypesIntro: Choose one or more. The questions are merged, and a question asked by two types is only asked once. If no template fits there is
requestSpec.chooseTypesOutro: , which asks the questions the templates would otherwise answer.
requestSpec.criteriaIntro: A criterion is good enough if an outsider can read it and answer yes or no. You approve every line — it is your specification, not the platform's. If you change a line the approval lapses, and the line must be approved again.
requestSpec.lede: The type of assignment decides which questions are asked, and the answers become the acceptance criteria both parties tick off. A request without a finalised specification is not open for bids.
requestSpec.publishIntro: After publication the wording is locked, and bids are bound to it. If something needs to change you open a revision — the current version remains in force until the new one is published.
requestSpec.questionsIntro: The answers are the basis for the criteria. A question may open a follow-up question — save, and it appears.
requestSpec.reviseIntro: A revision opens the next draft as a copy. Version {version} remains in force until you have published the new one, so bids that come in meanwhile refer to a wording that does not move.
requestSpec.title: Specification
